items.title: Conceptual Framework for a Virtual Symbiotic Environment for Maritime Operations Using Digital Twins and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Digital Twin technologies in maritime applications have primarily focused on individual subsystems, such as vessel machinery, navigation, or environmental monitoring, while limited attention has been given to the integrated representation of human operators, vessel dynamics, machinery, and environmental conditions. To address this challenge, a conceptual Virtual Symbiotic Environment for Maritime Operations (VSEMO) is proposed; the VSEMO integrates human, traffic, docking, environmental, and machinery Digital Twins within a closed-loop system engineering framework. The proposed architecture incorporates Explainable Artificial Intelligence to support transparent operational risk assessment and decision support, while immersive virtual reality provides a realistic environment for adaptive operator training. As an initial proof of concept, a Graph Convolutional Network is developed using synthetic graph-based operational scenarios to demonstrate the feasibility of jointly estimating subsystem-level and aggregate operational risk indicators. Although the computational implementation is limited to snapshot-based synthetic data, the proposed framework establishes a scalable and modular foundation for future real-time Digital Twin ecosystems that integrate physiological sensing, vessel telemetry, environmental information, and explainable artificial intelligence for maritime training and decision support.

items.title: Construcción subjetiva y evaluación del riesgo ocupacional en el proceso de empaque de banano en la agricultura familiar del Ecuador
items.abstract: The banana agro-export sector in Ecuador constitutes a decisive economic pillar, largely sustained by family farming and small-scale production. However, operational conditions in packing plants expose workers to multiple physical, biomechanical, and chemical hazards. This study analyzes the perception and level of occupational risk across the 8 activities of the packing process using the Dimensional Perceived Risk Assessment tool (EDRP-T), adapted from Technical Prevention Note (NTP) 578. A census population of N = 64 workers distributed across the operational stations was evaluated by applying 10 standardized criteria on a Likert scale (1–5). The results reveal a marked heterogeneity in the risk profile (Kruskal-Wallis H = 28.45, p < .001 for Severity). The De-handing and Selection (M = 3.80) and Bunch Reception (M = 3.70) activities recorded the highest levels of biomechanical risk and lacerations, whereas Fungicide Treatment and Immersion exhibited the highest perceived severity (C1 = 5.0) combined with the lowest personal control (C4 = 2.0). It is concluded that there is a normalization of musculoskeletal disorders and a critical dependence on institutional control measures regarding chemical hazards, leading to recommendations for ergonomic engineering interventions and technological substitution.

items.title: Contesting sociotechnical imaginaries: the technopolitics of artificial intelligence/cybersecurity convergence
items.abstract: The current development of artificial intelligence (AI) is sustained by powerful imaginaries that describe possible technological futures aligning with the normative preferences of influential actors. We show how an AI imaginary driven by “Big Tech” corporate interests and technosolutionism has influenced the development of an AI/cybersecurity imaginary in the UK. Building on the Science and Technology Studies concept of sociotechnical imaginaries, we adopt atechnopolitical lens to examine how external notions of AI progress and development interacted with internal U.K. government commitments to cybersecurity. Drawing on U.K. government texts and interviews with 37 officials, nongovernment experts, and industry actors, we trace the emergence of an AI/cybersecurity imaginary between 2022 and 2024, how intragovernment controversies were negotiated and resolved, and how this imaginary stabilised in U.K. security politics with identifiable outcomes in cybersecurity governance. The article contributes empirical support for the importance of sociotechnical imaginaries in understanding security trajectories, how corporate and technosolutionist imaginaries influence government policy and practice, and offer theoretical insights into the dynamics of imaginary formation and function. AI imaginaries promote the goals and values of science and technology, while technopolitics dominated by corporate actors and technoscientific optimism constrain governmental and social capacity to create and enact alternative imaginaries of future cybersecurity.

items.title: Conventional and Digital Prosthetic Appliances in Cleft Lip and Palate Care: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Cleft lip and palate (CL/P) are congenital craniofacial conditions that require coordinated, multidisciplinary care from infancy through growth. Presurgical orthopedic and prosthetic appliances, such as feeding/palatal plates and nasoalveolar molding (NAM) devices, are used in selected patients, and digital workflows based on intraoral or three-dimensional (3D) scanning, computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM), and 3D printing are increasingly proposed as alternatives to conventional fabrication. This study was conducted to map the available evidence on conventionally and digitally fabricated prosthetic and presurgical appliances for infants and young children with CL/P, to describe the characteristics of that evidence, and to identify research gaps. A scoping review was conducted and reported according to the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), using a Population–Concept–Context framework. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar were searched. Two reviewers screened records independently. Data were charted using a predefined set of items and summarized descriptively (counts and percentages) and narratively. No formal risk-of-bias assessment or meta-analysis was undertaken. Thirty sources were included: 7 systematic reviews (3 with meta-analysis), 1 randomized controlled trial, 2 observational clinical studies, 13 case reports, case series, or technical reports, 4 workflow-development or technical-validation studies, 2 in vitro studies, and 1 narrative review. Twenty-three sources (76.7%) were published in 2021 or later. By focus, 10 addressed feeding/palatal plates and obturators, 4 digital impression or scanning, 5 conventional NAM, 9 digital NAM or presurgical plate workflows, and 2 artificial intelligence (AI)-supported planning. items.title: Cooperative UAV and Ground Station for Robust MEC of Dynamic Aquatic IoT: A Generative AI-Enhanced Approach
items.abstract: The increasing aquatic Internet of Things (AIoTs) require computational support and coverage in applications such as maritime search and rescue. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can offer low-cost, flexible aerial services, and ground stations (GSs) can provide powerful supports, which can cooperate to help the AIoTs in complex scenarios. However, the collaboration between UAVs and GSs for AIoTs faces challenges of task uncertainties, AIoTs trajectory uncertainties, heterogeneities, and limited computational resources. To address these issues, we propose a cooperative UAV and GS based robust multi-access edge computing (MEC) framework to assist AIoTs in completing computational tasks. Specifically, we formulate the optimization problem of joint task offloading and UAV trajectory to minimize the total execution time, which is in the form of mixed integer nonlinear programming and NP-hard to tackle. Therefore, we propose the algorithm of generative artificial intelligence-enhanced heterogeneous agent proximal policy optimization (GAI-HAPPO). The proposed algorithm integrates GAI models to enhance the actor network ability to model complex environments and extract high-level features, thereby allowing the algorithm to predict uncertainties and adapt to dynamic conditions. Additionally, GAI stabilizes the critic network, addressing the instability of multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches. Finally, extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms the existing benchmark methods, thus highlighting the potentials in tackling intricate, cross-domain issues in the considered scenarios.

items.title: CoSlice: Coordinated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for 5G Network Slicing Allocation
items.abstract: Radio Access Network (RAN) slicing is a shared resource allocation problem: each slice seeks to satisfy its Service Level Agreement (SLA) with minimal radio-resource consumption, while all slices compete for a limited resource budget. This creates both an intra-slice trade-off between SLA assurance and resource efficiency and an inter-slice conflict over shared resources, calling for specialized yet coordinated control. In this work, we present CoSlice, a coordinated multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for inter-slice physical resource block allocation in Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN). CoSlice uses preference-conditioned slice agents for fast resource allocation and an LLM-based coordinator to adapt their objectives using global network observations at a slower timescale. We formulate the problem as a multi-objective partially observable stochastic game (mo-POSG), establish the existence of a Preference Correlated Equilibrium, and derive a sublinear regret bound for the learning procedure. We implement the algorithm by using a two-stage training procedure that consists of multi-objective pretraining and joint optimization. We build a network slicing evaluation environment using ORANSlice and its radio-frequency simulator (RFsim), supporting realistic protocol-stack execution and application traffic across multiple slices. Experimental results show that CoSlice reduces both average and tail SLA violations compared with other centralized and multi-agent baselines under diverse slice workloads.
topics: Cognitive Radio Networks and Spectrum Sensing

items.title: CounselTraj: Synthesizing Process-Aware Psychological Counseling Dialogues via Dialogue-Act Trajectory Planning
items.abstract: The growing demand for psychological counseling has motivated the development of LLM-based systems that support human counselors, but training such systems requires large-scale, high-quality dialogue data. Authentic counseling transcripts are difficult to collect and share because of privacy concerns, making synthetic dialogues an important alternative. However, existing synthetic datasets, despite covering diverse scenarios and client profiles, often consist of brief exchanges and fail to capture session-level counseling processes. We propose CounselTraj, a dialogue-act trajectory planning framework for expanding brief synthetic dialogues into process-aware, session-level psychological counseling dialogues. CounselTraj learns dialogue-act patterns from role-play counseling dialogues produced by human counselors, plans coordinated trajectories for clients and counselors, and uses them as flexible guidance for long-form dialogue generation. Experiments across three Chinese synthetic counseling datasets show that CounselTraj produces more complete and coherent sessions with higher-quality counselor interventions than both direct expansion and expansion with randomly sampled trajectories. Based on CounselTraj, we construct CounselTrajD, a dataset containing over 10K process-guided Chinese psychological counseling dialogues, and use it to train CounselTrajLM for counseling response generation. Evaluations at both the response and session levels show that CounselTrajLM outperforms publicly available Chinese counseling models in response quality, therapeutic understanding and intervention, and counseling-process coherence and progress. Our code and model are publicly available at https://github.com/UEC-InabaLab/CounselTraj.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

items.title: Crisis Governance at the Joints. Mapping the Ethical and Societal Territory of Crisis Management Technologies: The Case of Human-Swarm Teaming
items.abstract: Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of crisis governance. They promise better situational awareness in disaster response, but they also raise questions about human control, responsibility, surveillance, triage, dual use and public legitimacy. This report maps the ethical and societal territory that HST opens up. It unpacks this territory with a 3i-framework, the Interface, where operators and swarms work together, the Infrastructure, where organisations distribute tasks, decisions and blame, and the Imaginary, where law, policy and shared societal assumptions define what a crisis is and which interventions it justifies. The central claim is that these concerns cannot be addressed one level at a time. Many of the most pressing problems, such as responsibility gaps and the erosion of meaningful human control, arise at the joints between levels, through four translations, habits harden, routines become stories, principles become procedures, and procedures become prompts. Drawing on a critical review of literature across philosophy of technology, political theory, moral psychology, philosophy of mind, AI ethics, and critical disaster and security studies, the report develops this framework, illustrates it with two worked examples, and derives design and governance implications and a set of questions for developers, emergency organisations and policymakers.

items.title: Cross-domain encoding models reveal shared and domain-specific neural representations across language and mathematics
items.abstract: Whether language and mathematics rely on shared or distinct neural representations remains unresolved in cognitive neuroscience. Here, we combined latent features from a large language model with functional magnetic resonance imaging encoding models to test cross-domain generalization in 32 participants performing sentence comprehension and calculation tasks. Cross-domain prediction identified cortical regions showing partially shared representations, most consistently in the left area 55b, while control analyses suggested that these effects could not be fully explained by low-level visual or task-general factors. Domain-specificity contrasts revealed stronger language-related prediction in the left superior temporal sulcus and angular gyrus and math-related prediction in the left precentral sulcus and bilateral intraparietal sulci. Model-weight analyses revealed distinct weight profiles associated with shared and domain-specific prediction patterns. Cross-domain regions also exhibited task-dependent functional coupling with language- and math-related networks. Together, these findings suggest that language and mathematics involve partially shared neural representations alongside domain-specific cortical organization, helping reconcile previous contrasting views on their neural basis.

items.title: Cuando trabajar enferma: incumplimiento de normas de seguridad y salud laboral y sus consecuencias en el bienestar de los trabajadores
items.abstract: La existencia de normas de seguridad y salud laboral no garantiza que los riesgos ocupacionales estén efectivamente controlados. El objetivo fue analizar críticamente la evidencia sobre cumplimiento preventivo, exposición ocupacional y bienestar de los trabajadores, y formular un marco integrado de evaluación. Se realizó una revisión narrativa crítica mediante búsquedas web dirigidas a publicaciones académicas y fuentes institucionales, con verificación de metadatos en registros bibliográficos y sitios oficiales. Se seleccionaron veinte documentos por su pertinencia, diferenciando investigaciones, síntesis de evidencia y orientaciones técnicas. Los hallazgos muestran que determinadas inspecciones pueden reducir lesiones, que las condiciones laborales adversas se relacionan con problemas de salud física y mental y que la documentación resulta insuficiente para valorar la protección efectiva. La relación entre exposición y enfermedad no demuestra por sí sola incumplimiento jurídico ni permite atribuirle toda la carga de daño. Se propone un marco que distingue requisitos aplicables, controles operativos, exposición y resultados de salud, con participación de los trabajadores y seguimiento correctivo. Se concluye que la evaluación preventiva necesita integrar evidencia documental, condiciones reales de trabajo y bienestar. El alcance narrativo, el acceso desigual a textos completos y la ausencia de datos propios limitan la inferencia causal y la transferencia local.

items.title: Cultivating Effective Reading Habits in Higher Education: Challenges and Pathways to English Language Proficiency
items.abstract: Reading plays a fundamental role in the development of English language proficiency by enhancing vocabulary acquisition, grammatical knowledge, comprehension abilities, and critical thinking skills. Despite its importance, many university students encounter persistent challenges that hinder the development of effective reading habits and limit opportunities for meaningful language growth. This paper examines the major barriers affecting reading development among university students and explores how these challenges influence English language proficiency. Guided by Reading Engagement Theory and Self-Determination Theory, the discussion is organised around four interconnected dimensions: cognitive and affective barriers to reading development, reading culture and literacy support, literacy competence and advanced reading challenges, and pedagogical practices influencing reading engagement. The analysis suggests that reading anxiety, limited intrinsic motivation, dependence on extrinsic incentives, inadequate literacy support, vocabulary limitations, weak critical reading skills, and traditional instructional approaches collectively restrict students' reading development. Furthermore, excessive reliance on passive learning strategies and fragmented vocabulary instruction may impede learners' ability to engage deeply with texts and develop higher-order comprehension skills. The paper argues that successful reading development requires more than exposure to texts alone; it demands supportive learning environments, meaningful reading experiences, learner autonomy, and instructional approaches that promote active engagement. Strengthening reading culture, expanding opportunities for extensive reading, and fostering intrinsic motivation may contribute significantly to improved language proficiency and academic achievement. Future research should explore digital reading environments, reading engagement in multilingual contexts, technology-assisted literacy development, and the long-term effects of reading habits on language learning outcomes.

items.title: Cultural Bias and Representational Gaps in Conversational Generative AI for Mental Health: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Limited access to mental health support due to infrastructural limitations and workforce shortages has contributed to growing interest in the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for scalable mental health support. Despite their promise, these technologies pose risks, such as hallucinations and misalignment with local experiences of mental health challenges in the Global South. While there is growing attention to safety and harm mitigation, limited research has examined how cultural representation, linguistic coverage, and dataset provenance shape these technologies, particularly for Global South populations, and how cultural sensitivity can be improved to support mental health care. This systematic review synthesises 29 empirical studies published between 2020 and April 2026, predominantly concerning conversational GenAI for mental health. Using a keyword-based search strategy, critical narrative synthesis, and reflexive deductive thematic analysis, we examined how GenAI systems encode cultural assumptions. Our findings reveal representational gaps, limited culturally grounded narratives, and predominantly additive adaptation, whereby cultural elements are introduced while underlying Western diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks generally remain unchanged. Also, we consolidate cross-study evidence into strategies that have implications for clinical and non-clinical collaborative practices for mental health support. Lastly, we outline implications for Human-Centred AI and Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and directions for culturally grounded conversational GenAI that supports equitable mental health care.

items.title: Curriculum–Industry Alignment in Civil Engineering Education in the Philippines: Perspectives of Graduates and Construction Industry Practitioners on Competency Gaps and Future Workforce Needs
items.abstract: The rapid transformation of the construction industry driven by digitalization, sustainability requirements, and evolving project delivery methods has increased the need for civil engineering curricula that are responsive to industry demands. This study evaluated the alignment between civil engineering education and construction-industry requirements by comparing the perspectives of civil engineering graduates and industry practitioners. A cross-sectional descriptive-comparative research design was employed involving 127 respondents, consisting of 79 civil engineering graduates with less than three years of professional experience and 48 industry practitioners with more than three years of construction-related experience. Data were collected using a researcher-developed questionnaire covering four dimensions: curriculum relevance and adequacy, observed competency deficiencies, preparedness for emerging technologies and practices, and recommended curricular reforms. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Mann–Whitney U tests, weighted ranking analysis, and thematic analysis were performed. The instrument demonstrated excellent reliability, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.914 to 0.959. Results indicated that both graduates and industry practitioners perceived the current curriculum as insufficiently aligned with contemporary construction-industry needs and identified competency gaps primarily related to construction software proficiency, planning and scheduling, contract administration, and site supervision. Although respondents considered the curriculum to provide moderate preparation for emerging technologies, substantial gaps remained in areas such as Building Information Modeling (BIM), digital construction tools, artificial intelligence, data analytics, and reality-capture technologies. No statistically significant differences were observed between graduates and industry practitioners across the four assessment dimensions (p > 0.05), indicating a strong consensus regarding curriculum strengths, deficiencies, and future priorities. Internship and industry immersion programs, construction planning and scheduling, industry-based case studies, software training, and BIM education emerged as the highest-priority curricular reforms. The findings highlight the need for a more industry-responsive and technology-oriented civil engineering curriculum that strengthens experiential learning, digital competencies, and industry engagement to better prepare graduates for the evolving demands of the construction sector.

items.title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
items.abstract: A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. We introduce CurvDelta, a scalable framework that incorporates the preservation constraint into the parameterization of the model update. By analyzing the local geometry of the preservation constraint around the pre-adaptation model, CurvDelta constructs a low-curvature space in which parameter updates leave the preservation loss nearly invariant. We make its construction practical for LLMs through Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (K-FAC) and a factorized projection. We also introduce CurvLoRA, a low-rank variant within the same preservation geometry, designed for more efficient adaptation. Both methods apply to preservation-constrained adaptation tasks such as capability learning and selective unlearning. We evaluate our methods on mathematical reasoning, code generation, and knowledge unlearning. For mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approaches achieve competitive downstream performance while better preserving general capabilities, offering a favorable acquisition--retention trade-off relative to the baselines. For knowledge unlearning, our main results on TOFU and MUSE show a better balance between targeted forgetting and knowledge retention than the baselines, with retention performance close to the from-scratch retraining reference.

items.title: CyDeBoost: A SHAP-Guided Boosting Strategy Framework for Cyberbullying Detection through Mistake-Driven Learning
items.abstract: The widespread use of online social media has increased the urgency of detecting and mitigating harmful language, such as cyberbullying. Traditional detection systems often struggle with semantically ambiguous and context-dependent expressions, leading to frequent misclassifications. This article presents CyDeBoost, a mistake-driven boosting framework for cyberbullying detection. The core idea of CyDeBoost is to identify and learn from misclassified instances by leveraging SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to uncover key lexical features responsible for prediction errors. Based on these insights, the framework uses large language models to generate semantically contrastive augmented samples, which are then used to fine-tune the model through a modular continual learning strategy. Specifically, lightweight adapter modules are stacked iteratively to simulate the boosting process while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Experimental results demonstrate that CyDeBoost improves classification robustness across multiple cyberbullying categories and maintains generalization under low-resource settings. This framework aligns with the goals of content moderation on dynamic web platforms by offering interpretable, adaptive, and resource-efficient language safety solutions.

items.title: Data-Intensive and Ai-Mediated Anticipatory Governance: A Functional Typology of Institutional Capacity, Decision-Making, and Governance of Expertise
items.abstract: Anticipatory Governance (AG) has emerged as a strategic approach for addressing uncertainty, systemic risk, and complexity in contemporary socio-technical systems. Governments and universities increasingly rely on Big Data, Data Science, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support future-oriented public decision-making, yet the institutional and societal implications of these technologies remain conceptually fragmented. This article addresses this gap through a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) that examines how data-intensive and AI-enabled capabilities become embedded across foresight, knowledge creation, policy design, and policy assessment. Rather than treating the generic technical differences among Big Data, Data Science, and AI as the principal contribution, the study develops a functional typology that distinguishes infrastructural observation and evidentiary integration, analytical modeling and interpretation, and AI-enabled decision mediation. The review analyzes how these functions respond to uncertainty, non-linearity, interdependence, and feedback; reshape informational, analytical, and decisional capacity; and redistribute epistemic and decisional authority. The findings indicate a cumulative but non-deterministic movement from expanded observability, to analytical structuring, to increasingly mediated action. We conceptualize this movement as decisional embedding: the degree to which technological systems enter the institutional production of alternatives, prioritization, recommendation, adjustment, or execution. The contribution lies in showing that technological integration in anticipatory governance is not merely an increase in computational capability, but a reconfiguration of knowledge, judgment, responsibility, and authority. The article concludes with implications for accountable, contestable, and human-governed hybrid decision architectures.

items.title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult. We approach these challenges through a policy-induced capability region, the set of states from which the current policy can reliably complete a task. Near its boundary, an agent may need only a few actions to reach a more solvable state, even when the goal remains distant. This reduces long-horizon learning to two coupled subproblems of reaching that state and completing the task from there. We address them with paired advantages and a progressive reverse-to-forward curriculum. The advantages provide separate signals for reaching more solvable states and completing the task from them, while the curriculum expands the capability region backward along successful reference trajectories and then into off-reference states through on-policy exploration. On ALFWorld and WebShop, our method outperforms competitive agentic RL methods at both model scales, achieving success rates of 90.1%/96.1% and 80.2%/82.6% with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, respectively.

items.title: Depth-Gated Evidence Availability: How a Search Can Miss the Evidence Needed to Widen It
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Depth-Gated Evidence Availability, a mechanism through which the scope of a diagnosis determines what evidence an inquiry can obtain. An investigator who treats a model’s assumptions as settled can test different values within it while leaving those assumptions unexamined. This creates a particular difficulty when the evidence that would justify widening the inquiry depends on a comparison that the current inquiry has no occasion to make. The paper assesses a choice of diagnostic depth by asking what questions the current frame permits, what evidence would bear on a deeper alternative, and whether the present investigation could obtain it. To identify the mechanism, one must trace a specific gap in the evidence to a question the frame excludes and show how asking that question makes the evidence obtainable. A narrow investigation can still be proportionate to its purpose. The value and cost of the missing comparison matter when deciding whether to pursue it. The paper places the mechanism alongside Thomas Kuhn’s account of how paradigms guide the selection of scientific problems and examines two historical cases. In 1901, the Wright brothers’ glider produced about one-third of the lift they expected. Their wind tunnel allowed them to compare different wing shapes under the same conditions. The comparison supported Lilienthal’s measurements for his own wing and exposed a problem in applying them to the Wrights’ wings. In 1909, Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden asked whether alpha particles could return from a metal surface. A screen shielded from direct particles let them observe returns that earlier forward measurements could not register. Those observations later informed Ernest Rutherford’s proposal of a concentrated central charge. Part of the Recursive Inquiry and Encounter series within On Human Modeling, the paper has a potential application in human–AI evaluation. Reviewers who vary a prompt and score each answer may take for granted that the assistant received the relevant source passage. Asking which passages actually reached the assistant calls for a different record. That record lets reviewers distinguish a passage the system omitted from one it received and failed to use.

items.title: Designing the dialogue: A participatory study to develop AI-mediated architecture critiques
items.abstract: The pedagogy of the Architecture Design studio centers on iterative learning and critique, yet traditional review formats often induce information overload and psychosocial barriers for students. Concurrently, while artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in architectural education, its application remains largely instrumentcentric, acting as an assistant for early-stage ideation and technical optimization.This instrument-centric approach neglects AI's potential to support higher-order cognitive tasks and risks fostering passive learning. To address this gap, this study investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) can be repositioned as active "reflection partners" to mitigate the social pressure of critiques and scaffold objective, self-regulated learning across individual self-reflection, peer-to-peer critique, and professor-led critique. Using Participatory Design (PD) methodology, this study engaged 22 architecture students in a series of co-design workshops. Participants engaged in structured ideation and created low-fidelity, paper-based wireframes simulating AI-mediated interactions. The collected artifacts and sticky-note rationales were evaluated using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings reveal that students prioritize human-centered AI features that safeguard personal agency, including robust anonymity controls, intent-alignment checking to prevent AI from becoming a rigid evaluator, and multi-stakeholder role-playing simulations. These insights informed the conceptualization of "Studioboard, " a proposed LLM-integrated platform that synthesizes peer and professor critique, translates complex terminology, and tracks curriculum-level progress over time. The study concludes that user-designed, AI-mediated critique platforms can effectively neutralize the power hierarchies and social anxieties inherent in architectural reviews.

items.title: Detect What You Need: Chain-of-Causal Reasoning for 3D Intent Grounding
items.abstract: Accurately matching human intentions in 3D space is an important goal of artificial intelligence. Recently, 3D Intention Grounding (3D-IG) has emerged, aiming to localize target 3D objects given a natural-language intent. Unlike conventional visual grounding with descriptive referring expressions, 3D-IG intents are abstract and non-descriptive, making object localization substantially more challenging. This requires inferring latent functional requirements from non-descriptive intents and aligning them with object-level 3D representations. However, existing methods largely rely on implicit intent-object matching, leading to logical gaps and limited interpretability, robustness, and generalization. To address these challenges, we propose Chain-of-Causal Reasoning (CoCR), a causality-inspired functional dependency reasoning framework that explicitly bridges abstract intentions and candidate objects through intermediate functional requirements. Specifically, CoCR progressively decomposes complex intents into ordered functional requirements, thereby forming an explicit intent-function-object reasoning chain that links abstract intentions to object suitability. Building on this chain, we construct a causality-inspired functional dependency graph to model requirement-attribute relationships and introduce a causal-visual alignment module that aligns function-aware representations with the geometric-semantic features of 3D point clouds, enabling bidirectional verification between structured functional reasoning and visual evidence. Extensive experiments on 3D Intention Grounding and 3D Visual Grounding demonstrate that our method enhances intent-aware object localization. Our code is available at https://2490o.github.io/CoCR.

items.title: Digital Health Literacy and Verification of Sexual and Reproductive Health Information on TikTok: The Role of Artificial Intelligence Among Young People in Timor-Leste
items.abstract: Social media platforms, particularly TikTok, have become increasingly important sources of health information among young people. However, the accuracy of health-related content remains a concern, especially regarding sexual and reproductive health (SRH). The ability to evaluate online information and verify its credibility is therefore an essential component of digital health literacy. The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini, also provides new opportunities for users to seek additional explanations and verify health-related information. Nevertheless, the reliability of AI-generated responses requires critical evaluation. This study aims to examine digital health literacy and the verification of sexual and reproductive health information encountered on TikTok among young people in Timor-Leste, with particular attention to the use of AI tools. An analytical cross-sectional study will be conducted among young people aged 18–24 years who use TikTok in Timor-Leste. The study will target 200 respondents using a non-probability convenience sampling technique. Data will be collected through a structured, self-administered online questionnaire using Google Forms. The questionnaire will assess TikTok exposure to SRH information, trust in health-related content, information verification practices, digital health literacy, and the use of AI tools for health information verification. Data will be analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics to examine patterns of information verification and relationships among the study variables. The study is expected to provide evidence on how young people evaluate and verify SRH information encountered on TikTok and how AI tools contribute to their information-seeking practices. The findings may support the development of digital health literacy initiatives and promote responsible use of AI for health information among young people in Timor-Leste.

items.title: Dino-cd:marrying DINOv3 with dual-branch complementary reconstruction for remote sensing change detection
items.abstract: The goal of remote sensing change detection (RSCD) is to accurately distinguish land-surface changes. Recently, Vision foundation models (VFMs), such as the self-supervised DINOv3, have demonstrated strong semantic parsing capabilities across various visual tasks. However, directly applying DINOv3 to RSCD remains challenging. First, DINOv3 produces low-resolution, single-scale feature representations, which are unfavorable for pixel-wise change classification. Second, DINOv3 is not tailored for RSCD and thus struggles to model geospatial differences along the temporal dimension. To address these issues, Marrying DINOv3 with Dual-Branch Complementary Reconstruction for Remote Sensing Change Detection (DINO-CD) is proposed. Specifically, a dual-branch complementary reconstruction module is introduced to enable interaction between DINO and CNN branches for complementary feature enhancement, producing multi-scale representations that preserve global semantic consistency while strengthening local detail discrimination. In addition, a hierarchical difference aggregation module is designed to comprehensively enhance temporal discrepancies via explicit frequency learning and multi-scale directional aggregation, thereby highlighting effective change regions and reducing false alarms and missed detections. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate that DINO-CD outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving gains of 6% in F1-score and 8% in IoU on the CLCD dataset.

items.title: Disenchanting the Epistemic Authority and Inevitability of AI: An Analysis of Factcheckers’ Perspectives and Professional Guidelines
items.abstract: As a sociotechnical practice, fact-checking integrates artificial intelligence (AI) while resisting “enchanted determinism” to preserve professional agency and epistemic authority. This study examines how fact-checkers in Europe and Latin America perceive AI affordances within their professional practices and how organizations articulate and govern AI use. Methodologically, the study is based on 50 qualitative interviews with practitioners and a thematic analysis of 18 publicly available AI guidelines and institutional documents. The findings suggest a distinction between instrumental optimism and epistemic disenchantment . While fact-checkers embrace AI’s functional affordances to enhance efficiency in tasks such as monitoring and data processing, they resist delegating the authority to determine truth to autonomous systems. At the organizational level, human-in-the-loop requirements formalize this distinction and operate as a form of boundary work that defines the limits of automation. We also identify a shared rationale for AI use across countries, which may reflect some degree of institutional convergence. However, this consensus coexists with a persistent “AI divide” shaped by contextual forces. Overall, the study shows how fact-checkers act as sociotechnical agents who “strip the magic” from AI, reaffirming human judgment as the field’s core epistemic foundation.

items.title: Dissecting an Unexplored SASS Control-Code Field: Barrier Exemption and Programmable Warp Priority
items.abstract: Every instruction in NVIDIA's native GPU ISA (SASS) carries a control code that guides hardware scheduling, and prior work has decoded its known fields to optimize GPU kernels. However, one control-code field remains unexplored: it appears over 500000 times in NVIDIA's closed-source libraries such as cuBLAS and cuDNN, yet nvcc never emits it when compiling user programs. This paper presents the first systematic study of this control-code field across GPU architectures from Volta to Blackwell. Using instruction-level microbenchmarks, we show that the field controls two independent hardware mechanisms: barrier exemption (EXEMPT), which allows instructions blocked by a pending barrier to issue early during the barrier wait, and programmable warp priority (START, TILE, and END), which moves warps across three priority levels in the hardware scheduler. We identify the conditions under which each mechanism improves GPU kernel performance and implement a post-compilation binary optimizer that places these marks directly in compiled binaries without modifying source code or the compiler. Evaluated across six GPUs spanning four architectures, our optimizations speed up representative kernels by up to 31.9%, and the optimizer accelerates production kernels in llama.cpp and vLLM by up to 5.4% and end-to-end LLM inference by up to 3.6%.

items.title: Do Metrics for Counterfactual Explanations Align with User Perception?
items.abstract: Explainability is widely regarded as essential for trustworthy artificial intelligence systems. However, the metrics commonly used to evaluate counterfactual explanations are algorithmic evaluation metrics that are rarely validated against human judgments of explanation quality. This raises the question of whether such metrics meaningfully reflect user perceptions. We address this question through an empirical study that directly compares algorithmic evaluation metrics with human judgments across three datasets. Participants rated counterfactual explanations along multiple dimensions of perceived quality, which we relate to a comprehensive set of standard counterfactual metrics. We analyze both individual relationships and the extent to which combinations of metrics can predict human assessments. Our results show that correlations between algorithmic metrics and human ratings are generally weak and strongly dataset-dependent. Moreover, increasing the number of metrics used in predictive models does not lead to reliable improvements, indicating structural limitations in how current metrics capture criteria relevant for humans. Overall, our findings suggest that widely used counterfactual evaluation metrics fail to reflect key aspects of explanation quality as perceived by users, underscoring the need for more human-centered approaches to evaluating explainable artificial intelligence.

items.title: Early feedback elicitation and downstream participation behaviours: a retrospective observational analysis of study completion and disengagement
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Many health research studies and clinical trials face threats to external validity and low statistical power because they are unable to recruit and retain a sufficient number of participants. Identifying study design improvements using participant feedback is an important avenue through which studies seek to address these challenges. However, the returns on this approach have been limited because experience measures are rarely linked to actual participation behaviour. We examine whether feedback collected at the beginning of a research study can provide a meaningful signal about future participation as measured by study completion, withdrawal, and communication unsubscription. METHODS: We use observational data from a large health research program (N = 35,838; 77% from groups historically underrepresented in biomedical research, UBR) in which feedback was collected across the participant experience. We correlate feedback responses (e.g., indicating satisfaction with the experience) with study completion and active disengagement 6 months later and use Artificial Intelligence (AI) processing of free-text comments to surface specific topics and sentiment. FINDINGS: Ratings given immediately after onboarding are associated with an 8.89 percentage-point (pp) higher study completion rate ('Good' vs 'Fair') and a 23.22 pp higher active disengagement rate ('Poor' vs 'Fair') within 6 months. Associations for feedback collected later are smaller (up to 4.17 pp for completion). These differences hold after adjusting for participant characteristics (age, income, educational attainment, sex at birth, UBR on race/ethnicity, and UBR on rurality). We find no statistically significant effect of the prompt itself. AI-extracted topics and sentiment agree with human reviewers 86% and 81% of the time, respectively. INTERPRETATION: Early, light-touch feedback can meaningfully differentiate participants by their likelihood of completing or disengaging from a study, creating opportunities to target support and address flagged concerns while the study is still in progress. Feedback collected at the end of a study is a weaker signal of future behaviour. Our approach, including AI processing of free-text comments, is readily portable to other studies and feedback elicitations. Whether feedback-informed changes improve retention is an important question for future work. FUNDING: National Institutes of Health.

items.title: Eco-AI: Artificial Intelligence Framework for Predicting and Reducing Carbon Emissions in Depok City
items.abstract: Depok City faces increasing carbon emissions associated with rapid urbanization, a population exceeding 2.7 million, and more than 821,000 registered motor vehicles. However, the city lacks an integrated, data-driven framework for predicting greenhouse gas emissions and evaluating emission reduction strategies. This study aimed to develop Eco-AI, an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework designed to predict greenhouse gas emissions and assess mitigation strategies in Depok City through the integration of multiple predictive and optimization models. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining quantitative and qualitative analyses using Internet of Things (IoT) sensor measurements (MQ-135 and SDS011), Sentinel-5P satellite observations, and administrative data from relevant government agencies, including DLHK, Dishub, PLN, and BPS. Five AI models were incorporated: long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for time-series forecasting, random forest (RF) for identifying influential emission-related factors, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) for emission hotspot classification, graph neural networks (GNNs) for spatial analysis, and reinforcement learning using proximal policy optimization (PPO) for policy scenario optimization. The results indicated that Depok City's total greenhouse gas emissions reached 4,217,340 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO?e) in 2024, with transportation accounting for 43.2% and residential energy consumption contributing 29.9%. The LSTM model achieved strong predictive performance (R² = 0.924; mean absolute percentage error [MAPE] = 4.97%), while the RF model identified the number of motor vehicles as the most influential predictor (feature importance = 0.234). Under the business-as-usual (BAU) scenario, annual emissions were projected to reach 5,891,200 tCO?e by 2030. The combined mitigation scenario indicated a potential emissions reduction of 19.1% relative to the BAU projection, with an estimated investment requirement of IDR 1.24 trillion. These findings suggested that the Eco-AI framework could support data-driven emissions forecasting, identification of emission-related factors, spatial assessment, and evaluation of mitigation strategies. The framework may contribute to evidence-based urban climate planning and support Depok City's efforts toward Indonesia's national net-zero emissions target for 2060.

items.title: EcoNav AI: An AI-Powered Disaster Assistance System with Offline Chatbot and Navigation
items.abstract: Natural disasters frequently damage mobile towers and power supply, leaving affected people without internet access ex-actly when they need maps, first-aid instructions and a way to call for help. Most disaster-management applications depend on cloud services and centralized networks, so they fail under these conditions. This paper presents EcoNav AI, an offline-first mobile disaster assistance system that integrates (i) an on-device AI chat-bot for emergency and first-aid guidance, (ii) GPS-based navigation over pre-downloaded OpenStreetMap data, (iii) locally stored infor-mation on shelters, hospitals, food and water points, (iv) a one-tap SOS alert carrying the available GPS location, and (v) peer-to-peer messaging over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and Wi-Fi Direct. All data are held in a local SQLite database so that core functions work without a network. We survey twenty recent studies on dis-aster communication, AI-based decision support and situational awareness, identify the lack of an integrated, resource-efficient offline platform, and propose a modular architecture together with Level 0 and Level 1 data-flow models, a local data schema and hardware/software requirements. This work reports the design stage (Phase I); implementation and field evaluation are planned as future work

items.abstract: This study investigated the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted instruction on students’ achievement and interest in Basic Science and Technology in secondary schools in Imo State, Nigeria. It also examined gender differences in achievement and interest among students exposed to AI- assisted instruction. The study adopted a quasi- experimental, non- randomized pretest- posttest control group design. The study involved 120 Junior Secondary School Two (JSS II) students drawn from four public secondary schools, with 60 students in the AI- assisted instruction group and 60 in the conventional teaching group. Data were collected using the Basic Science and Technology Achievement Test (BSTAT) and the Basic Science and Technology Interest Scale (BSTIS).

items.title: Effectiveness of exercise therapy in managing low back pain among industrial workers: a protocol of a systematic literature review
items.abstract: Low back pain is among the most common and debilitating musculoskeletal disorders worldwide, with industrial workers particularly at risk due to high physical demands and biomechanical stressors in their work environments. Despite broad evidence supporting exercise therapy for managing low back pain in general populations, the effectiveness and applicability of structured exercise programs among industrial workers remain underexplored. This systematic review aims to evaluate the effectiveness of exercise-based interventions specifically targeting non-specific low back pain in industrial settings. This systematic review will encompass randomized controlled trials and controlled quasi-experimental studies that examine structured exercise interventions, such as strength training, core stabilization, or motor control therapy among adult industrial workers with non-specific low back pain of any symptom duration (acute < 6 weeks, subacute 6–12 weeks, or chronic > 12 weeks). Eligible studies must compare exercise interventions with usual care, non-exercise controls, or other types of exercise programs. Primary outcomes are pain intensity and functional disability, with short-term follow-up as the primary time point. Secondary outcomes are work participation (return-to-work and absenteeism), recurrence, quality of life, work ability and adverse events. The search strategy will involve a three-step process: initial exploratory search in PubMed, comprehensive database searching using identified keywords and index terms, and manual reference list screening. Databases to be searched include PubMed, CINAHL, CENTRAL (Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials), SCOPUS, and ProQuest for gray literature. Two independent reviewers will screen articles using Rayyan software, extract relevant data using a standardized form, and assess methodological quality using validated tools. Randomized and quasi-experimental studies will be synthesized separately, and a narrative synthesis will be performed in accordance with the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) reporting guideline. The review will provide a focused synthesis of the evidence regarding the effectiveness of structured exercise therapy in managing low back pain among industrial workers. It aims to summarize the existing evidence and may help identify implications for occupational health practice and priorities for future research, particularly regarding longer-term outcomes and implementation in high-demand labor environments. items.title: Effects of acupuncture-assisted power nap on presenteeism, fatigue, and psychomotor vigilance in female workers with self-reported fatigue: a randomized controlled trial
items.abstract: Background Fatigue and presenteeism are major contributors to productivity loss and have become important targets of occupational health and health and productivity management programs. Although power naps are known to reduce fatigue and improve alertness, whether acupuncture enhances these effects remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether acupuncture-assisted power naps could improve work performance outcomes beyond the effects of power naps alone in female workers with self-reported fatigue. Methods Sixty-one female workers with self-reported fatigue from seven companies and healthcare institutions in Japan were randomized to the power nap group ( n = 29) or the acupuncture-assisted power nap group ( n = 32). Two randomized participants did not receive the allocated intervention or provide post-baseline outcome data; consequently, 59 participants (28 and 31, respectively) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. Participants received a 20-min power nap twice weekly for 8 weeks, with the intervention group receiving acupuncture during the nap period. The primary outcomes were subjective fatigue, assessed using the Japan National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health Fatigue Checker, and psychomotor vigilance, measured using the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT). The prespecified secondary outcome was presenteeism (absolute and relative presenteeism), assessed using the World Health Organization Health and Work Performance Questionnaire. Absolute and relative absenteeism were additionally analyzed as exploratory outcomes. Outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Results No significant group-by-time interactions were observed for fatigue ( F = 0.79, p = 0.457) or PVT reaction time ( F = 0.62, p = 0.543). In unadjusted analyses, significant group-by-time interactions were observed for absolute ( F = 7.92, p < 0.001) and relative presenteeism ( F = 3.65, p = 0.029). In adjusted sensitivity analyses, the interaction remained significant for absolute presenteeism ( F = 9.57, p = 0.003) but was no longer significant for relative presenteeism ( F = 2.11, p = 0.152). In exploratory analyses, no significant group-by-time interactions were observed for absenteeism. Conclusion No additional benefit of acupuncture-assisted power naps over power naps alone was demonstrated for short-term fatigue or psychomotor vigilance. Favorable findings for presenteeism were observed in secondary analyses, but these findings were attenuated after adjustment, particularly for relative presenteeism, and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. items.title: El uso de la tecnología educativa en la enseñanza de la geología en Educación Secundaria Obligatoria y Enseñanza Universitaria
items.abstract: The use of educational technology has transformed teaching and learning methods, particularly in disciplines such as geology. The main aim of this study is to analyze the application of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), including Artificial Intelligence (AI), in the classroom and to assess its impact on academic performance and student motivation in the teaching and learning of geology in compulsory secondary education and higher education. The study consisted of a systematic literature review of 25 scientific publications using PRISMA 2020. The results indicate that educational technology complements conventional teaching methods through simulations, interactive resources, and virtual environments, and promotes understanding of abstract concepts and meaningful learning. However, several barriers to integration remain, including insufficient teacher training, resistance to methodological change, and limited infrastructure and access to technology.

items.title: Emo-H2A: Driving a Facial Robot Directly from LLM Hidden States at Token Rate
items.abstract: Diverse, semantically synchronized, and low-latency facial expressions are essential for human-robot interaction. While large language models (LLMs) have endowed anthropomorphic robots with fluent speech, facial expression still struggles to follow the conversation. Motivated by this gap, we present Emo-H2A (hidden-to-actuation), a paradigm that drives a facial robot directly from LLM hidden states during autoregressive decoding. Without a separate emotion label, expression stays continuous and context-sensitive, and the face moves with the unfolding reply. We instantiate this paradigm as EmoManifold, a training-free method that extracts a valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) coordinate from each hidden state, projects it, and drives the face at token granularity. The readout is checked on six language models, and the same projection drives our 29-degree-of-freedom (DoF) facial robot. When driven by this projection, the face shifts its expression in the matching direction on 87.5% of within-reply valence transitions, whereas holding a single label for the whole reply leaves directional tracking near the 50% chance level, and first moves in 0.96s rather than waiting 10-26s for the reply to finish and a turn-level label to return.

Conventional viral vectors and synthetic nanocarriers are associated with challenges including immunogenicity, limited cargo capacity, prolonged nuclease expression, off-target effects, and manufacturing complexities. Engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) are being investigated as alternative delivery carriers due to their biological origin, capacity for cargo encapsulation, and opportunities for surface functionalization. We discuss the advantages and limitations of different CRISPR cargo formats, including plasmid DNA, mRNA, and ribonucleoprotein complexes, together with endogenous and exogenous loading approaches, hybrid EV platforms, and methods for enhancing intracellular delivery. Advances in EV surface engineering through genetic, chemical, physical, and biomimetic modifications are highlighted as strategies being investigated to improve tissue-specific delivery and functional cargo transport. The review also highlights emerging research directions, including CRISPR-EV theranostic platforms and the application of artificial intelligence to enhance CRISPR-EV therapeutic systems. Finally, key translational challenges, including scalable production, EV heterogeneity, cargo-loading efficiency, biodistribution, regulatory standardization, and quality control, are critically discussed. EV-mediated CRISPR delivery remains at an early preclinical stage, with clinical safety and therapeutic efficacy yet to be established. Further advances in EV engineering, cargo-loading strategies, and manufacturing standardization are needed to support its potential clinical translation.

items.title: Enhancing Pedagogical Practices Through Generative AI: Recommendations for DepEd Policy Development
items.abstract: This study examined public-school teachers’ readiness, utilization, challenges, and ethical practices regarding generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) in the Department of Education–National Capital Region (DepEd NCR), with the aim of developing policy recommendations for responsible and equitable classroom integration. Guided by the Technology Acceptance Model, the research employed an embedded mixed-methods design using questionnaire responses from 454 teachers across 16 school divisions and in-depth interviews with 18 educators during academic year 2024–2025. Quantitative responses were analyzed descriptively, while qualitative interview accounts were organized through thematic analysis to contextualize teachers’ experiences. The findings described moderate teacher readiness and uneven use of Gen AI, with applications more evident in lesson planning and instructional preparation than in assessment and student engagement. Participants identified insufficient training, unequal connectivity and device access, curriculum-alignment concerns, and uncertainty about ethical responsibilities as important constraints. Teachers also described efforts to verify AI-generated content, protect student information, and preserve instructional judgment. Based on the combined evidence, the study proposed a policy framework emphasizing differentiated professional development, infrastructure support, ethical safeguards, implementation monitoring, and sustained teacher participation. The November 2026 publication update situates these 2024–2025 findings within subsequently issued national guidance, without treating the update as new empirical data.

items.title: Ergo Analyzer: Ergonomic Risk Assessment System Using Computer Vision & REBA
items.abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders remain a leading cause of injury and lost workdays in manufacturing, yet ergonomic assessment on the shopfloor is still largely periodic, manual and subjective. This paper presents Ergo Analyzer, a contactless, camera-based system that converts ordinary video into real-time, actionable ergonomic insight. The framework detects workers in the video stream, estimates seventeen body keypoints using a real-time pose estimation model, computes joint angles and body alignment, and compares them against ergonomic thresholds. A machine learning classifier then assigns a color-coded risk level and a numerical score from zero to one hundred, together with body region sub-scores for the back, shoulders, wrists and legs. A recommendation engine converts the result into task-specific corrective feedback such as adjusting posture, raising the work surface or taking micro-breaks. A prototype built with Python and OpenCV and exercised in simulated shopfloor conditions assigned distinct risk levels to good posture, improper lifting and excessive bending, and, in a live qualitative demonstration, the risk score fell from 72 to 32 after the recommended posture was adopted. We describe the architecture, scoring method, implementation and limitations, and outline a validation plan and roadmap toward alerts, mobile applications and wearable integration

items.title: Ergonomics of Manual Material Handling in Construction: A Systematic Review of Assessment Tools, Wearable Monitoring, and Intervention Effectiveness
items.abstract: Purpose: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) due to manual material handling (MMH) are an important and widely documented occupational health burden that is common in construction, manufacturing and heavy industrial sectors worldwide. This review of assessment tools examines sensor-based monitoring and intervention outcomes in manual material handling (MMH) in construction. Design/Methodology/Approach: Through a systematic search method compliant with PRISMA 2020, we examine the peer-reviewed literature published from 2010 to 2023 as contained in six electronic bibliographic databases, namely, Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed/MEDLINE, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, in five domains regarding wearable and mechatronics-based monitoring interventions for work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) which are the prevalence of WMSDs in the workplace, assessment instruments for measuring physical exposure to biomechanical risk factors, effectiveness of interventions, and Axiomatic Design which helps design and structure the above-mentioned interventions. Of the 1,847 records initially retrieved, 51 studies fully met the eligibility criteria after duplicate removal and sequential screening. Research Limitation: Five interrelated research gaps are identified: integrated multi-tool assessment frameworks for construction MMH, cost-appropriate sensor instrumentation, formal design methodology application, longitudinal intervention validation, and India-specific ergonomic guidelines. Findings: The low back (median prevalence 76%), neck (60%) and shoulder (55%) were the anatomical sites with the most consistent injuries across industry. The Rapid Entire Body Assessment was the most commonly used assessment tool, appearing in nearly seven in ten included studies, and scores for construction-related tasks were uniformly between 8 and 13 in the high-risk to very-high-risk action categories. The wearable sensor systems estimated the L5/S1 spinal compression force with error within ±8.3% of laboratory optoelectronic reference systems. This indicates sufficient fidelity for deployment in the field; however, the estimated cost of validated commercial systems is USD 15,000-100,000 which limits access for small and medium enterprises. The most effective risk reduction was achieved with a combination of engineering and administrative ergonomic control interventions, as indicated by declines of 41–55% in REBA scores. Furthermore, the results indicated a 38–49% reduction in the prevalence of WMSD symptoms across 31 intervention studies included in the systematic review. Practical Implication: A five-phase mechatronics-Axiomatic Design framework is proposed to address all five gaps within a single coherent research architecture. Social Implication: The findings support mandatory site-level ergonomic assessment and low-cost interventions to reduce chronic musculoskeletal pain among construction workers, particularly in the informal sector. Originality/Value: To the authors' knowledge, this is the first systematic review to integrate assessment-tool performance, wearable sensor monitoring, intervention effectiveness, and Axiomatic Design in a single synthesis for construction MMH, and the first to propose a five-phase mechatronics-Axiomatic Design framework tailored to Indian construction.

items.abstract: Nine verification reports can represent nine independent observations or nine copies of one. This technical working paper measures how much fresh evidence a recursive learner receives, how much survives five training updates, and when trusting faulty source identifiers increases predictive error. Across 20 paired simulation trials, correct source identification retained a predictive advantage of 11.95 percentage points of baseline risk after five updates. Exact enumeration gives break-even case-corruption rates of 29.5% to 50.2% under two specified fault mechanisms. The eight-page paper includes three figures and reproducible Python experiments. Working with ChatGPT (OpenAI) has helped me expand my strategic thinking, examine competing explanations, and connect my proposals to relevant scientific and technical research. items.title: Ethical and practical challenges of artificial intelligence for sleep and mental health in disability care: a narrative review
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored to support sleep and mental health care, yet its role in disability care remains insufficiently synthesised. This narrative review examines the ethical and practical challenges associated with AI applications for sleep and mental health in disability care, with attention to both people with disability and disability support workers. Current applications include wearable and sensor-based sleep monitoring, mood tracking systems, conversational agents, predictive models, and workforce-facing decision-support tools. These technologies may improve early detection, continuous monitoring, personalised support, and care coordination. However, the literature identifies substantial barriers to safe and equitable implementation. Practical challenges include poor accessibility, limited inclusive usability, workflow disruption, variable digital literacy, weak external validation, and concerns about reliability across diverse disability groups. Ethical concerns include privacy and data governance, meaningful informed consent, algorithmic bias, lack of transparency, intrusive surveillance, and the risk of dehumanising care. The evidence base is also limited by overreliance on general mental health AI literature, minimal focus on disability support workers, a lack of longitudinal and implementation research, and insufficient co-design with people with disability. Overall, AI may offer meaningful benefits in disability care, but responsible implementation requires disability-specific evidence, inclusive design, strong governance, human oversight, and sustained commitment to person-centred and rights-based care.

items.title: Ethical bricolage as ethics-as-practice in criminal organizations. The case of a drug dealing gang
items.abstract: In this paper, we explore how ethics emerge in contexts of criminal organizations. To do so, we carried out a non-participant observation of a suburban drug dealing gang. Resorting to Lévi-Strauss’ concept of “bricolage”, we posit that actors assemble and recombine available moral resources in practice. We found that the criminals we studied resorted to various practices of ethical bricolage, which we define as a genuine mode of social organizing resulting from individuals collectively mobilizing and recombining available moral resources to promote situated ethical practices aimed at designing and maintaining a delineated moral territory. We contribute to the ethics-as-practice literature in discussing how, in organizations lacking social acceptability, ethical bricolage constitutes a mode of organizing, structuring the boundaries of a “man-made” acceptable life.

items.title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality
items.abstract: Video evaluators play an important role in video generation, yet they miss motion defects, limiting the quality of generated videos. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) has made strong progress in mathematics and coding, where explicit verifiers provide reliable feedback on a single goal. Video evaluation poses two difficulties for RSI: it has no verifier, and it must judge many dimensions at once, such as physics, smoothness and dynamics, where a gain on one can cost another. We introduce EVA-RSI, a multi-agent framework for exploring RSI under these two constraints. We build a fixed proxy exam with construction-defined targets by applying controlled changes to videos, such as temporal reversal and frame dropping. These edits supply supervision without human annotation. A small set of human-labeled real videos anchors the exam to human judgment. Each dimension has an LLM agent that proposes improvements. A leader agent coordinates the proposals, and a Nash bargaining rule selects updates that balance progress across dimensions. Humans design the exam, review candidate changes and revise the curriculum between stages. Starting from Qwen3-VL-8B, EVA-RSI improves motion evaluation, with the largest gain on smoothness, and the gains carry over to defect types never seen during the run. On the dynamics subsets of public benchmarks, our evaluator achieves the highest observed scores among 21 tested models. As an RL reward, it increases generated motion and earns human preference. A data-selection pipeline incorporating it also increases motion.
